justification: CVE-2025-53649 affected the SwitchBot App for iOS and Android (V6.24 through V9.12), where sensitive user information was written to application log files recoverable by any local actor with log access (CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File). The synthetic vulnerability in Jerboa replicates this exact attack class: the vulnerability.patch removes the sanitizeHeader configuration from Jerboa's Ktor HTTP client Logging plugin. With sanitizeHeader removed and the log level set to ALL, the Authorization header containing the user's JWT Bearer token is written to Android logcat on every authenticated request. An attacker with adb access or READ_LOGS permission can extract the token from logcat and use it to call the Lemmy API on the victim's behalf, reading private messages and other authenticated resources. Both CVE-2025-53649 and this synthetic vulnerability follow the same pattern: a mobile app fails to redact sensitive authentication material from its logs, exposing session credentials to local privilege boundaries.
